headline: Sequence models and multiomic evidence are combined to score noncoding variant effects in cell-type context
label: Regulatory Variant Effect Prediction
summary: New tools fold Enformer outputs, methylation, 3D genome and single-molecule accessibility into variant prioritization across tissues and cell types.
synthesis: The dominant thread is prioritizing noncoding regulatory variants by combining sequence-based predictions with functional genomic context. eQIF compresses Enformer predictions into a single unsupervised isolation-forest score per common variant for eQTL and GWAS prioritization. mV2G integrates 24 evidence types across 50 tissues with a CRISPR-informed model, and Wreath extends variant effect prediction to DNA methylation using a compendium spanning over 90 tissues and cell types. Cell-type specificity is addressed through CellReg3D (DNA language model embeddings with Hi-C), CNN-CR (compact shared promoter motif families across 116 biosamples), and XGBoost-SHAP on pancreatic progenitor snATAC-seq for HNF4A motif effects. Mola moves the prediction target to single-molecule chromatin accessibility distributions. The sex-biased enhancer study adds tissue-level regulatory context relevant to variant interpretation.
